apparatus.basis: Editor restoration completing the iterative cosmological formula: each element gathers inward to its like-element. The pattern (light → fire, fire → fire, water → water, wind → wind...) is cosmologically standard, with the construction parallel to lines 30 and 31.

Editor restores [ⲧⲏ]ⲩ; the word ⲧⲏⲩ in this context is uncertain. Could be 'winds/spirits' or part of a longer absolute pronoun (e.g. ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ 'all'). The translator's tentative gloss is 'all' as the lowest term in the cosmic ascent-chain.
ⲛ̄ⲧⲉ genitive linker, lost letters reconstructed from continuation.
Standard ⲁ-ⲡ directional preposition + article, completing 'gathered to'.
ⲡⲥⲧⲩⲗⲟⲥ ⲙ̄ⲡⲉⲁⲩ 'the Pillar of Glory' — standard Manichaean technical term.
Repeated ⲡⲥⲧⲩⲗⲟⲥ ⲙ̄ⲡⲉⲁⲩ 'the Pillar of Glory'.
ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ 'the First Man,' standard Manichaean cosmogonic figure (in glossary as ⲡⲱⲁⲣⲡ ⲛⲣⲱⲙⲉ).
ⲁⲛⲁⲓⲱⲛ 'Aeons' — restoring the initial alpha. Note: transcription shows '[ⲁ]ⲛⲁ]ⲱⲛ' with stray bracket; read as ⲁⲛⲁⲓⲱⲛ.
ⲉⲩⲛⲁⲥⲱⲩϩ 'they shall gather' — restoring future tense circumstantial converter.
ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲧⲡⲉ 'the upper place' (in glossary). Standard cosmological term.

notes.decision: Coptic numeral ⲟⲁ = 71 (ⲟ=70 + ⲁ=1). Treated as the chapter number (kephalaion 71) marked decoratively at the head of the new chapter title. Lines 25-27 together form a chapter-heading frame: line 25 isolated chapter-number above, line 26 the title proper, line 27 title continuation flanked by chapter-number marks.

'The gathering-inward' — verbal noun from ⲥⲱⲟⲩϩ 'gather' + ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ 'inward.' Same root as ⲣⲉϩⲥⲱⲩⲍ ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ 'the Gatherer-Inward' in glossary. Translated to preserve the cosmological inward-motion of cosmic light-recovery — each element drawn back to its source-element.
'He said' — Lycopolitan reflex of ⲡⲉϫⲁϥ. The chapter opens with the standard Kephalaia narrative-frame formula 'Once again the Illuminator said.'

'To the fire of the fire' — the cosmic principle that each element gathers to its self-same source-element. Direct correspondential identity: each manifest element returns to its primordial elemental form.

Transliterated as 'the Tamr' — an unidentified Manichaean technical term. The lexeme is unattested in our glossary; possibilities include (a) ⲡⲧⲁⲙⲏⲣ̄ qualitative of ⲙⲟⲩⲣ 'bind' = 'the bound one' (cosmologically the captive light/soul); (b) ⲡⲧⲁⲙⲟ-related 'announcement/instruction'; (c) a corrupt or specialized Lyc. form. Its position in the ascent-chain (between [ⲧⲏ]ⲩ and the Answer) suggests a low cosmic stage. Flagged for parallels.

Editor's restoration. The lone word ⲧⲏⲩ in this position is ambiguous — could be 'wind/spirit,' or part of an indefinite/absolute pronominal form. Translated tentatively as '[all]-y' to flag the uncertainty: this is the lowest term of the cosmic ascent-chain.

Greek loanword νοερόν 'noeric, intellectual.' Retained as 'the Noeric' to preserve the Greek philosophical register, paralleling the gloss given by the text itself ('the chosen Mind, which is the Noeric').
